summary: Zhigansk Airport (ZIX/UEVV) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the remote settlement of Zhigansk in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russian Far East. Situated near the Lena River in one of the coldest inhabited regions on Earth, it provides a vital air link for this isolated community where road access is essentially nonexistent. The airport primarily handles regional flights connecting Zhigansk to Yakutsk and other Yakutian settlements.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Zhigansk Airport?
A: The airport provides essential air connectivity for the remote settlement of Zhigansk, as the area has no road or rail links to other populated regions. It supports passenger travel, mail delivery, medical evacuations, and supply transport for the community.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Zhigansk?
A: Regional carriers such as Polar Airlines and other Yakutian aviation operators typically serve Zhigansk with scheduled passenger flights, primarily connecting to Yakutsk.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Zhigansk?
A: Winter operations (roughly November through April) generally offer the most reliable schedules, as extreme summer temperatures can occasionally affect small aircraft performance, though the airport operates year-round.

Q: How long is the flight from Yakutsk to Zhigansk?
A: The flight from Yakutsk to Zhigansk typically takes approximately 2 to 2.5 hours by regional aircraft.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few kilometers from the village center, and passengers typically reach the terminal by personal vehicle or pre-arranged local transport, as there is no public bus service. Taxis may be limited, so arranging ground transport in advance through your hotel or host is strongly recommended. Given the extreme climate, allow extra time for travel to the airport during winter when road conditions can be challenging.
local_tip: Pack a warm-layer outfit even in summer—temperatures can drop unexpectedly, and the airport terminal has limited amenities, so bringing your own snacks, water, and entertainment is wise for potential weather-related delays.
